subject: Outcome-based marketplace pricing & reseller profit-share proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@cloudbroker.io
Date: 2027-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace pricing idea — outcome / reseller share

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement is taking a hard look at list-price private offers because our internal procurement team wants predictable monthly spend tied to business outcomes (we measure active AI sessions per week).

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood structure a private offer that charges us based on “active sessions” tiers (outcome-based) rather than pure token consumption?
- We’d also like to keep our reseller (CloudBroker) motivated — they’re asking for a margin share on any upsell/overage. What would an acceptable reseller profit-share look like when the marketplace only supports SKU-based billing?

If you’re open to a short call, happy to walk through their commercial constraints.

Jordan
Procurement, Acme Enterprises

(Attachment: ACME_RFP_summary.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, partners@cloudbroker.io
Date: 2027-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing idea — outcome / reseller share

Jordan —

Really appreciate the clarity here. Short answer: yes, we can model an outcome-based commercial even when the marketplace requires SKU mapping, but there are a few operational constraints and margin implications to align on.

High-level approach we propose (draft):
1) Map outcome tiers to SKUs: create 3 discrete SKUs (baseline, scaled, overage) that mirror active-session bands (e.g., 0-5k, 5k-25k, 25k+ active sessions/month).
2) Set a blended unit price per SKU that approximates your target effective $/session.
3) Implement a reseller profit-share as a % of net revenue attributable to overage SKU usage only (so baseline is protected).

Questions for Acme to confirm:
- Target effective $/active-session at each tier (we modeled $0.30 baseline, $0.22 scaled, $0.16 overage for a starting point).
- Will you accept monthly reconciliation (marketplace invoices + our overlay settlement) or do you require immediate pass-through splits on the invoice?

Ben / Karthik / Irene — please see Jordan’s ask and my proposed approach. Can you weigh in on feasible reseller split mechanics (marketplace billing + Redwood settlement) and an initial margin split we should propose to CloudBroker?

I’ll attach a scenario workbook with modeled outcomes for Acme to review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

All — quick take from channel/comp perspective.

We need a structure that is easy for CloudBroker to explain and that doesn’t create undue accounting churn for Acme. Two practical options:

Option A — Overage-only reseller share (preferred):
- Baseline SKU: list price covers Redwood cost + 10% partner fee (no split). Protects customer predictable bucket.
- Overage SKU: 70% Redwood / 30% CloudBroker of net revenue (after marketplace fees).
- Settlement: Redwood issues a monthly settlement to CloudBroker for overage share; Acme gets a single invoice from marketplace.

Option B — Tiered share that ramps with volume:
- Baseline: 95/5 (Rdwd/partner) up to scaled tier
- Scaled: 85/15 between scaled and overage
- Overage: 70/30 beyond 25k sessions

Key operational considerations (Irene to confirm):
- Marketplace SKU naming must match billing events exactly (we can’t split a single invoice line into two parties). That’s why we map to three SKUs and do post-invoice settlement.
- Taxes and remittance: partner will need a subcontract that allows Redwood to remit the share; this adds ~45–60 days to partner payment cycles.
- If Acme requires immediate split on the invoice (marketplace pass-through), we lose settlement control and margins compress by marketplace fees.

I think Option A is easiest and cleanest for all parties. Karthik — can you run the modeled margin impact for Redwood (assume our effective unit cost at $0.08/session for baseline compute + infra amortization)? I’ll add a brief note to the Acme proposal recommending Option A for simplicity.

-Ben
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Jordan / CloudBroker team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on internal alignment, here's a concrete proposal for Acme to review:

Summary (short):
- We will map your outcome tiers to three marketplace SKUs (Baseline, Scaled, Overage) that correspond to bands of active sessions/month.
- Pricing (starting example): Baseline $0.30/session, Scaled $0.22/session, Overage $0.16/session.
- Reseller profit-share: 30% of net revenue attributable to Overage SKU only (Redwood 70% / CloudBroker 30%). Baseline and Scaled remain as single-party billed to Redwood to keep predictable pricing for Acme.
- Settlement cadence: monthly settlement from Redwood to CloudBroker for Overage share (standard 45-day payment term).

Operational notes:
- Marketplace requires SKUs; we will create named SKUs and attach the private offer. Acme will be invoiced by the marketplace for the SKUs consumed; Redwood will provide a monthly settlement statement and remit the overage share to CloudBroker.
- If Acme prefers immediate pass-through on marketplace invoice, we can explore that, but it will reduce the partner share by ~3–5% due to marketplace transaction fees and add bookkeeping complexity.

Next steps:
1) Jordan — confirm the three session bands above or provide your preferred bands.
2) Jordan — confirm you accept monthly settlement rather than invoice pass-through.
3) Marissa & Ben will update the attached proposal and send a tracked DocuSign for a private-offer order form if items 1–2 are OK.

Attachments: Redwood_outcome_pricing_v2.pdf (walkthrough), acme_pricing_model_scenarios.xlsx (scenarios showing effective $/session across usage shapes).

If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize bands.

Thanks,
